Kaprekar's Iterations

ArithmeticAlgorithmsInvariants
Game: Sort a number's digits, subtract, and see which constant the process reaches.
How to play: Set the start, base and width, then press Step or Run to reveal the chain.
Look for the math

Nearly every four-digit number falls into the same trap after a handful of steps.

The process

Arrange the digits largest-first and smallest-first, then subtract. Kaprekar found that padding short differences with zeros makes every four-digit number except repdigits (1111, 2222, …) reach 6174, where 7641 − 1467 = 6174. With three digits the constant is 495. The logic test checks all 9,990 non-repdigit four-digit starts: every one reaches 6174 in at most seven steps.

Why padding matters

Without padding, 1121 gives 2111 − 1112 = 999, and the next subtraction is zero. Padding turns it into 9990 − 999 = 8991, which continues to 6174. Other bases have their own constants: base 8 with three digits reaches 252, while base 5 with three digits has no single constant.

Try a number with all digits equal, then one that differs by just one. What changes when you uncheck padding?
